newsitem.title: USA: CBOE starts trading warrants on Japan export index.
newsitem.headline: CBOE starts trading warrants on Japan export index.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange opened trading on Wednesday in Japan Export Index call warrants which expire March 29, 1999, the exchange said.
The index .JEX is a new stock index made up of 40 stocks that are among the largest Japanese export companies as measured by total export revenue over the last five years.
The offering of one million call warrants was underwritten by Oppenheimer & Co, ING Barings and Peregrine Capital.
Volume totaled 35,000 and the warrants closed at 5-5/8, their session high. They hit a session low of 5-1/2.
Kessler Asher is the Designated Primary Market Maker for the new warrants, the CBOE said.
The JEX ended 3.93 points up at 236.07.

The CBOE said the cash settlement value of a warrant will be based on a formula that calculates the appreciation of the index level and then divides by a fixed yen-dollar rate of 122.25 yen per dollar.
Ben Krause, senior managing director of CBOE Capital Markets, said in a statement the new warrants give investors the chance to participate in the stock activity of large Japanese companies.
